title: SparkLend sources liquidity directly from Sky rather than from depositors, so it can undercut market borrow rates
content:
A.6.1.1.1.1 describes SparkLend as "a lending market focused on USDS borrowing, sourcing liquidity directly from Sky to provide the best borrow rates for USDS."

The mechanism is the interesting part. A conventional DeFi lending market must attract supply from depositors, so its borrow rate is bounded below by whatever yield depositors demand; utilization spikes force rates up. SparkLend inverts this by taking its USDS supply from the issuer itself. The rate becomes a **policy choice** by Sky rather than the output of a deposit auction.

That is what makes "the best borrow rates for USDS" a structural claim and not marketing: no competitor sourcing from third-party depositors can systematically match a rate set by the entity that mints the asset.

The trade-off is where the risk moves. Because Sky is the supplier, borrower defaults and market shocks are absorbed by the ecosystem's balance sheet rather than by unrelated depositors. Subsidized borrow rates are therefore an expenditure of Sky's risk capacity, which is why lending exposure has to be governed by explicit parameters elsewhere in the Artifact rather than left to the market.
description: A lending market whose supply side is the issuer itself is not rate-constrained by competing for deposits — the structural reason Spark can claim the best USDS borrow rates.
